newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends sharply off on Kurdish truce.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends sharply off on Kurdish truce.

text.p: NYMEX crude ended almost a $1.00 lower Thursday, sending gasoline and heating oil down with it, on news rival Kurdish factions in Iraq agreed to extend a U.S.-brokered ceasefire, renewing hope for an Iraqi oil-for-food deal, traders said.

"We are moving to a new and lower trading range (for crude) near term of between $21.50 and $24.00. This Kurdish ceasefire is suggesting to the market that the oil-for-food deal could be expedited," said Sweeney Oil trader Jim Ritterbusch.
December crude ended off 93 cents at $23.35 a barrel.

Crude fell as much as $1.03 on news the Kurdistan Democratic Party and the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan agreed to end two months of clashes in northern Iraq and said they would not drag Iraq and Iran into their feud.

November heating oil fell 2.12 cents to 66.34 cents a gallon while November gasoline settled down a steep 3.44 cents a gallon at 66.56 cents. November refined product contracts posted the sharp losses before expiring at Thursday's close.
The selling in crude accelerated after Dec crude fell below $24.00, triggering sell stops, traders said, and they added crude is expected to test a gap which starts at $22.85.
"It was a lot of technical selling. After it went below $24.00, a bunch of stops went off," said MPAS Inc president Bob MacMinn of Thursday's price action in crude.

Crude's price gap on a continuation chart extends to $22.25 and occurred in early September when the United Nations suspended the Iraqi oil-for-food deal when Baghdad intervened to aid one of the Kurdish factions.
The deal would allow sales of up to $2 billion of oil over six months to pay for humanitarian relief.
Meanwhile, some traders said there was little downside left in heating oil, with good support seen at 66.00 cents a gallon.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
